nodes.name: Sunlight
nodes.desc: Light reaching the forest floor and canopy drives plant growth through the short northern summer.

nodes.name: Gauja River and springs
nodes.desc: The park follows the old valley of the Gauja River, with springs and sandstone cliffs. Water and wet floodplain soils feed riverside trees.

nodes.name: Soil nutrients
nodes.desc: Nutrients released from dead wood, leaves and carcasses are taken up again by forest plants.

nodes.name: Decomposers
nodes.desc: Fungi, bacteria and invertebrates break down dead wood, leaf litter and carcasses and return nutrients to the soil.

nodes.name: Scots pine
nodes.desc: A common conifer of sandy and sandstone soils in northern Europe. Its seeds feed red squirrels and its shoots are browsed by moose in winter.

nodes.name: Aspen
nodes.desc: A fast-growing riverside and forest tree. Beavers fell it and moose and hares browse its bark and twigs.

nodes.name: Bilberry
nodes.desc: A low berry shrub of the forest floor, recorded in the park. Its leaves and berries are eaten by deer, hares and foraging omnivores.

nodes.name: Bird cherry
nodes.desc: A small tree of moist floodplain woods, well recorded in the park. Its fruit and twigs feed many animals.

nodes.name: Eurasian beaver
nodes.desc: Eats bark, shoots and water plants, and fells trees such as aspen and willow. Its dams make wetlands used by otters, voles and bats; it is also prey for wolves and sometimes lynx.

nodes.name: Moose
nodes.desc: The largest deer in the region; browses twigs, bark and shoots of pine, aspen and other trees and shrubs. A main prey of wolves.

nodes.name: European roe deer
nodes.desc: Small deer that feeds on grass, leaves, berries and young shoots. It is the preferred prey of lynx where common, and is also taken by wolves.

nodes.name: Wild boar
nodes.desc: An omnivore that roots in the forest floor for plant matter, berries and invertebrates. One of the main wolf prey animals across Eurasia.

nodes.name: Eurasian red squirrel
nodes.desc: Feeds largely on conifer seeds such as pine. Recorded in the park and preyed on by pine martens.

nodes.name: European hare
nodes.desc: Grazes grasses and herbs and browses twigs in winter. Prey of foxes, lynx and wolves.

nodes.name: Red fox
nodes.desc: Hunts hares and young deer and scavenges carcasses. Also eaten by lynx where it is common.

nodes.name: European pine marten
nodes.desc: A forest-dwelling mustelid that hunts squirrels and small animals and also eats berries.

nodes.name: Raccoon dog
nodes.desc: An introduced omnivorous canid recorded in the park. Eats berries, small animals and carrion, and is taken by lynx.

nodes.name: Common raven
nodes.desc: A widespread scavenger of the northern forest that feeds on carrion, including the remains of wolf and lynx kills.

nodes.name: Eurasian lynx
nodes.desc: Ambush hunter that prefers roe deer where they are common. When roe deer are scarce it turns to hares, beavers, foxes and raccoon dogs.

nodes.name: Gray wolf
nodes.desc: Preys mainly on moose, roe deer and wild boar across Eurasia, and also takes beavers and hares. Competes with lynx for prey.
